quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride to the left or right of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors give you a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should only be used when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still do not see them.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold firmly to the operator's waist or midsection. They can also use handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: One problem with riding directly next to another vehicle is that:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read roadside signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a turn. Taking a turn too fast may cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What is the correct way to position yourself to control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to support your weight. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced when turning.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medications, can have side effects that affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication might affect your riding.

questions.question: When can you use a motorized bicycle or moped in a bicycle lane?

options.text: Only when you are carrying a passenger.
Only if your local laws or law enforcement allow it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if your local laws or law enforcement allow it.
questions.explanation: You can use a motorized bicycle or moped in a bicycle lane only if local laws or law enforcement permit it.

questions.question: What should you do differently when stopping your motorcycle with a passenger?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond to your actions. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when changing lanes or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a protective jacket for riding?

options.text: A jacket made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: A jacket made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms and fits snugly but lets you move freely. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with built-in body armor provide the best protection.

questions.question: Which lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from squeezing into your space. When following a car, riding in the center makes you more visible in the car's rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should you secure a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Secure it as low as possible.
Secure it as high as possible.
Attach it to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible. Do not attach loads to a sissy bar because it raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and affects its balance.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to be effective?

options.text: Limit your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resistant to breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to flow to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should you check when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It has no cracks or defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching intersections.

questions.question: When a motorcycle is towing a trailer, should the following distance increase or decrease?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Not at all, it is unsafe

questions.correctAnswerText: Together with the rear brake
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Most crashes between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. The main cause is car drivers failing to give the motorcycle the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a protective jacket?

options.text: It fits loosely and flaps in the wind
It fits snugly without flapping in the wind
It is not made of leather or sturdy material

questions.correctAnswerText: It fits snugly without flapping in the wind
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket made of leather or sturdy material. It should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: Are footrests required on a motorcycle?

options.text: They can be shared by the driver and passenger
Yes, they are required for both driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required for both driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing prevents your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe
Only stop to let other traffic pass
Other vehicles are entering the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians go, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When being passed, where in your lane should you ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: How should you brake during a normal, non-emergency stop?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: What is the best way to cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Slow down on the road shoulder before crossing
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks
Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight ahead in your lane to cross
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled tracks while staying in your lane. Changing your angle could push you into another lane and cause a collision.
